bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: In VPA, climaxes are defined strictly from the perspective of market insiders (specialists, market makers, and large institutional operators) rather than retail traders, designating when insiders are actively buying or selling.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: This book is written from the perspective of the insiders, the specialists, the big operators and the market makers... When I describe and write about a selling climax, to me, this is when the insiders are selling.

facts.statement: A selling climax occurs at the top of a bullish trend during the distribution phase, where insiders clear out their remaining inventory at high retail prices by selling to greedy retail investors driven by FOMO.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A selling climax appears at the top of the bullish trend... It is the culmination of all their efforts, and is the point at which the warehouse is almost empty and requires one last big effort to force the market higher.

facts.statement: A buying climax occurs at the bottom of a bearish trend during the accumulation phase, where insiders buy up massive stock inventory at wholesale prices from panicked retail traders who are capitulating.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: When the market has moved sharply lower in a price waterfall and a bearish trend, supported by masses of volume, this is a buying climax. It is the wholesalers who are buying and the retail traders who are panic selling.

facts.statement: The selling climax is characterized by high to ultra-high volume paired with candlesticks having deep upper wicks and narrow bodies, showing insiders pushing prices higher early to trap FOMO buyers before selling heavily.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Here we will see high volume coupled with a candlestick which has a deep upper wick and narrow body... The insiders are having one last effort to clear their inventory and mark prices higher early in the session.

facts.statement: The buying climax is characterized by high to ultra-high volume paired with hammer candlesticks having deep lower wicks and narrow bodies, where insiders absorb panic selling and push prices back up near the open.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The buying climax is simply a selling climax in reverse. The insiders have taken the market lower, panic has been triggered and fearful sellers are closing positions.

facts.statement: When institutions or market makers need to execute massive block orders without crashing or spiking public exchange prices, they utilize dark pools—private execution venues that hide large transactions from public view until completed.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: When institutions or market makers need to execute massive block orders at the top or bottom of a market, placing a single order on an open exchange would collapse or spike the price... institutions utilize dark pools.

facts.statement: Rogue trader Nick Leeson faced the classic institutional execution dilemma where his positions were so gigantic that unwinding or accumulating orders moved the market violently against his own execution prices, ultimately bankrupting Barings Bank.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Rogue trader Nick Leeson... faced the classic institutional execution dilemma. His positions were so gigantic that it became impossible to unwind them without moving the market violently against his own buying and selling.

facts.statement: Because buying or selling in extreme volume naturally drives prices in the opposite direction of institutional intent, climaxes cannot be completed in a single session and must be spread across multiple sessions.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Because buying or selling in extreme volume naturally drives prices in the opposite direction of what insiders want, climaxes cannot be completed in a single session. Insiders must spread their buying or selling across two, three, or four+ sessions.

facts.statement: The complete market cycle moves through six sequential phases: Accumulation, Buying Climax & Supply Test, Marking Market Up, Distribution, Selling Climax & Demand Test, and Marking Market Down.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The complete market cycle moves through six sequential phases: Accumulation Phase, Buying Climax & Supply Test, Marking Market Up, Distribution Phase, Selling Climax & Demand Test, Marking Market Down.

facts.statement: Coulling compares market cycles to a helter-skelter: markets climb the stairs slowly in steps during upticks to build confidence, but slide down fast on a mat ('down by the elevator') during panic liquidations.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Coulling compares market cycles to a fairground helter-skelter... Markets climb the stairs slowly in steps... but slide down fast on a mat/helter-skelter during panic liquidations.

facts.statement: Market cycles are fractal and exist simultaneously across all timeframes, mirroring nested Russian Matryoshka dolls where a 1-minute cycle sits inside a 15-minute cycle, which sits inside a daily cycle.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Market cycles are fractal and exist simultaneously across all timeframes (a 1-minute cycle sits inside a 15-minute cycle, which sits inside a daily cycle).

facts.statement: VPA operates under Wyckoff's Three Laws: Supply and Demand dictate direction, Cause and Effect dictate trend extent based on consolidation time/volume, and Effort vs. Result equate volume to effort and price spread to result.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Wyckoff's 1st Law (Supply & Demand)... Wyckoff's 2nd Law (Cause & Effect)... Wyckoff's 3rd Law (Effort vs. Result).

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
